newsitem.title: USA: Boehringer Mannheim says FDA approves device.
newsitem.headline: Boehringer Mannheim says FDA approves device.

text.p: Boerhringer Mannheim Corp said Wednesday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved its device that allows people taking blood thinners to monitor themselves at home.
The company said the device is called the coaguchek system for prothrombin time self-testing.
Boerhinger Mannheim said it is a privately held company.

The company said numerous studies indicate people participating in self-testing of blood thinner therapy remain within the correct therapeutic range more often than patient who follow traditional methods or monitoring.

The company said it also provides patients and physicians with a management system for the coaguchek through alliances with St. Jude Medical Inc and DuPont Pharma, two companies that are involved in blood thinner therapy.
The company said more than 1.5 million people take blood thinners, which helps prevent strokes and congestive heart failure.
